text:
Parker Kelly was never drafted, started his NHL career in Ottawa, and is now a fourth-line regular on a contender. Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe summed up his season in a headline on Nov. 13: "Parker Kelly Wanted to Prove the Senators Wrong. He Did." Fittingly, his best and worst moments of the month came in the same game in Ottawa on Nov. 12: a shorthanded goal off the rush, then a turnover in overtime that set up the winner.

He has 4 goals and 9 points in 21 games on 13 minutes a night, close to last season's pace, when he scored 21. He's shooting 17%, a little above what his chances explain, so expect the goals to come a touch slower.

The reason he plays is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.5 wins last season, 93rd among forwards, and opponents got fewer expected goals with him on the ice than with almost any other forward (98th percentile), though he played with strong teammates. The Denver Post reported Colorado building another strong fourth line around him and Logan O'Connor; that kind of trio is how good teams win nights their stars don't.
